name: Karma Guen
aka: Fundación Karma Guen Karma Kagyu Camino del Diamante
Karma Kagyu Diamond Way Buddhist Retreat Center Karma Guen
tradition: Diamond Way Buddhism, a lay Buddhist movement within the Karma Kagyu school of Tibetan Vajrayana Buddhism
technique: Guru yoga meditation on the 16th Karmapa; Ngöndro foundational practices; Vajrayana empowerments and initiations (e.g. Green Tara, Chenrezig, Kalachakra) from visiting lamas; Buddhist philosophy study through the ITAS program
teacherAccess: Daily meditations and the Sunday introductory lecture are led by resident practitioners and traveling students of Lama Ole rather than a resident teacher; direct teachings and empowerments from senior Karma Kagyu lamas (e.g. Jigme Rinpoche, Jamgon Kongtrul Rinpoche, Sherab Gyaltsen Rinpoche) are concentrated in periodic multi-day courses, not personal interviews
retreatOptions: Free weekly public meditation evenings and a Sunday 11am introductory lecture with meditation; personal open or closed retreats in an on-site meditation cave or a room (closed retreats longer than 3 days require guidance from one's own teacher); multi-day residential courses through the year (e.g. Easter course, 8th Karmapa/Autumn course, occasional Summer course), typically 5-10 nights, camping-based, drawing international students
about: Karma Guen is a Diamond Way Buddhist retreat center in the Axarquía hills above Vélez-Málaga in Andalucía, Spain, built from Aldea Alta, an abandoned mountain village bought by Dorrit and Pedro Gomez in the 1970s and given to the Karma Kagyu lineage at the wish of the 16th Karmapa, transmitted through Lama Ole and Hannah Nydahl. It is one of more than 700 Diamond Way centers founded by Lama Ole Nydahl worldwide, now under the patronage of the 17th Karmapa, Thaye Dorje, and practice follows the lay, non-monastic Diamond Way style: guru yoga meditation on the 16th Karmapa, Ngöndro foundational practices, and periodic empowerments and teachings from visiting Karma Kagyu lamas. Regular free meditations and a Sunday introductory lecture on Buddhism run alongside personal open or closed retreats (a meditation cave beside the on-site Kalachakra Stupa, or a room) and larger multi-day residential courses such as the Easter course and the 8th Karmapa/Autumn course, which draw international students for camping-based stays. Karma Guen also houses the ITAS academic programs founded by Hannah Nydahl in 2003 - Buddhist philosophy study courses, a Tibetan translation project, and a thangka-painting school - giving it an unusual dual identity as both meditation retreat and center for Tibetological study. Overnight and retreat stays are restricted to practicing Diamond Way Buddhists; casual visitors are welcome mainly on Sunday open days or public meditation evenings.
schedule: Daily Ngöndro session at 8am and public 16th Karmapa meditation at 8pm (in Spanish on Tuesdays); Sunday 11am introductory lecture on Buddhism followed by meditation; several multi-day residential courses per year (Easter, Autumn/8th Karmapa, occasional Summer course) with an intensive daily program of teachings, meditation and empowerments led by visiting Karma Kagyu lamas
cost: Regular meditations and the Sunday lecture are free; multi-day courses require paid online registration with price categories not published publicly, plus optional airport/bus shuttle (€15-35 per person) and camping-gear rental (tent, mat, sleeping bag); casual overnight or personal-retreat stays are arranged individually by email and restricted to Diamond Way Buddhist practitioners
foodNotes: During multi-day courses a volunteer kitchen team provides three meals a day to everyone registered to stay on site (using disposable dishware); food is not included for people who aren't registered to stay, though meals can be purchased separately, and cooking on one's own is prohibited during courses due to fire risk.
workNotes: Multi-day courses recruit volunteer 'helpers' through an on-site Job (Joy) Center to run logistics, but the website does not state a mandatory work requirement for all guests the way some other Diamond Way centers do.
